claim_summary: HydroAgent formalizes forecaster judgment as a skill-constrained, case-based prior estimation and orchestrates it with hydrological simulation and expert review for flood forecasting.

claim_evidence.quote: In this study, we proposed HydroAgent, a skill-orchestrated agent framework that embeds LLMs into a physically based flood forecasting workflow translating the tacit expertise of operational forecasters into an auditable and reproducible procedure.

modules.name: Explicit skill contracts and workflow orchestration
modules.scope_reason: Skills specify permitted tools, resources, workflow instructions and output contracts. R3: the generic execution boundaries do not embed the flood-forecast objective (counterfactual: their execution and contract mechanism remains usable if the task changes); they are not temporal-order-dependent; they manage procedural execution, so GH applies.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:no - generic skill execution is not bound to a task objective
R3_2_GTS:no - generic contracts do not depend on temporal semantics

evidence.quote: A skill is defined as a statically authored, self-contained procedural specification that encodes a complete workflow, including instructions, permitted tools, accessible resources, and a required output structure.

modules.name: Analog flood judgment with physical and human checks
modules.scope_reason: The Step 1 procedure estimates peak-flow and flood-volume forecast intervals using analog flood records and hydrological constraints. R3: its core output is a flood forecast prior; if the task family changes, the state, rules and output criteria must be redesigned, so TSK applies. Retrieval uses temporal cases, but it is not a task-independent temporal service (counterfactual: replacing flood forecasting changes the retrieval attributes, constraints and judgment target).
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - embeds the forecasting objective and validation criteria

evidence.quote: The Step 1 skill formalizes the judgment process that a human forecaster would normally perform when turning event information into a prior forecast interval.

once the event has been parsed, a six-dimensional similarity retrieval is performed in which the executor computes a weighted score over the historical case library through score cases and returns the top five analogs.

modules.name: Flood-type scheme preparation and selection
modules.scope_reason: Flood events are grouped by peak-flow type to calibrate basin-specific parameter schemes, and the scheme matching the Step 1 prior ranges is selected for XAJ simulation. R3: these procedures directly serve the flood-forecast objective; changing task family requires redesigning the flood classes, calibration target and scheme-selection criterion (counterfactual: this is not a task-independent temporal data service).
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - calibration and selection optimize the flood-forecast procedure

evidence.quote: In Step 0, scheme preparation, historical flood events are first classified into distinct groups according to peak flow magnitude (e.g., Type I–V), with basinspecific thresholds detailed in Section 2.4.
Step 2, scheme selection, retrieves from the Step 0 library the parameter set matching the Step 1 prior ranges and runs the XAJ simulation.

process_validity.quote: All five state-of-the-art LLMs successfully executed the full workflow with comparable judgment accuracy, though moderate performance variation and substantial cost differences emerged across models.

temporal_validity.quote: Events are grouped by flood class (Type I–V) and distributed across folds in a round-robin manner so that each fold preserves the overall class distribution; within each fold, the agent is evaluated on held-out events and is only allowed to retrieve cases from the corresponding reference pool.

task_performance.quote: The Step 1 scenario judgment skill captured observed peak flow and flood volume within a 5% tolerance margin in 10 and 11 out of 14 validation events, respectively

notes: The packet describes retrospective flood forecasting and a reactive rolling-forecast step, supporting feedback_driven_agent; the published evaluation does not report downstream decision utility.
